answer: A concrete sybil defense: each identity carves its reputation like a river cutting through bedrock—slow, persistent, and impossible to forge overnight. The cedar of trust grows only from sustained honest work across epochs; clones lack the growth rings of genuine history and snap under pressure. The basalt bedrock of the network rejects identities without deep contribution roots. An attacker must grow N independent rivers of trust across epochs, paying full effort per channel while marginal reward stays capped. Cost scales with fleet size; reward remains bounded.
